content.value_statement: Teams need reliable source discovery before scraping or answering questions. This skill guides Firecrawl search integration, result selection, and follow-up extraction decisions.
actual_capabilities: Guides query-first product flows that need Firecrawl /search before extraction.
Separates search discovery from scraping, interaction, and content hydration.
Recommends selective follow-up extraction to reduce cost and latency.
Points developers to language-specific Firecrawl documentation for integration code.
Maps search results into shortlists for citations, research, and downstream scraping.
limitations: It does not implement Firecrawl API calls by itself.
It requires a valid Firecrawl API key for hosted requests.
It does not automatically validate result quality, ranking bias, or source credibility.
It relies on external Firecrawl documentation for language-specific code details.

use_cases.title: Build Search-First Answers
use_cases.description: Design a feature that discovers current sources before generating cited answers.

use_cases.title: Shortlist Research Sources
use_cases.description: Turn a topic query into candidate pages before deeper extraction or review.

use_cases.title: Route Agent Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose when an agent should search, scrape, or interact with a page.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Search Or Scrape
prompt_templates.prompt: I am building a feature that starts with a user query. Decide whether to use Firecrawl /search first or direct scraping, and explain the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Result Selection
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Firecrawl search flow for this product feature: [describe feature]. Specify what results to keep, when to hydrate content, and what to return.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Extraction Follow-Up
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a search-to-extraction plan for [topic]. Separate discovery, ranking, scraping, and citation steps so the downstream workflow stays predictable.

prompt_templates.title: Review Search Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this proposed Firecrawl search integration for cost, latency, credential handling, and routing between search, scrape, and interact skills.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks for current, cited answers to customer questions.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: start with Firecrawl search, select relevant URLs, then scrape only the strongest sources for cited answers.

output_examples.input: A developer already has the exact article URL to process.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: skip search and use the scrape workflow, because discovery is not needed.

output_examples.input: An agent must compare competitors from a plain-language query.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: search first, rank candidate company pages, then extract details from the selected results.

best_practices: Use search when the workflow starts with a query instead of a known URL.
Separate discovery, source selection, and extraction steps in the product design.
Limit hydration and follow-up scraping to results that are likely to be useful.
anti_patterns: Using search after a known target URL is already available.
Hydrating every search result when snippets and URLs are enough.
Mixing search, scraping, and page interaction without clear routing rules.

faq.question: Does this skill call Firecrawl directly?
faq.answer: No. It guides implementation decisions and points to Firecrawl documentation.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Hosted Firecrawl workflows require FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, but the skill itself does not store credentials.

faq.question: Can it replace scraping?
faq.answer: No. Search finds candidate pages, while scraping extracts content from selected pages.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it work with self-hosted Firecrawl?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill mentions FIRECRAWL_API_URL for self-hosted deployments.

faq.question: Does it guarantee current results?
faq.answer: No. Result freshness depends on Firecrawl search behavior and the wider web.
